messages:
maya: Heads-up 3:30 sync takeaways on Console saved filters presets. High-level: keep model-level presets authoritative; routes reference them and only store small deltas. Need concrete API sketch + rollout plan.

sam: Sounds sane. Key thing: quota/cost preview and historical telemetry must reflect the merged, run-time effective query, not just the base preset. Otherwise cost estimates will be wrong.

liam: Agreed. Implementation note: avoid full-copy semantics. Store references + delta operations to minimize duplication and make updates predictable.

ana: UX question: when a route inherits but tweaks one filter, how do we show that in the Console list? We shouldn't flood the saved list with near-duplicates.

maya: Option: show the preset name with a subtle "override" pill. Clicking opens a diff panel that highlights the changed filters/columns. Rename only if user explicitly saves-as-new.

jordan: API sketch idea: extend saved_query with two fields: scope=("model"|"route"), source_id (when scope=route, points to model preset), and deltas array. Example payload (as a string sample in the UI):

```json
{
  "id": "sq_route_987",
  "scope": "route",
  "source_id": "sq_model_22",
  "deltas": [
    {"type": "replace_filter", "filter_id": "f_age", "payload": {"op":"gt","value":30}},
    {"type": "add_column", "name": "token_cost"}
  ]
}
```

jordan: The backend would materialize the merged query at preview time and return an `effective_hint` object containing model suggestion and merged filters for display.

sam: For routing policies, if the runtime chooses a different model during request time (policy-based fallbacks, multi-model routing), we need the preview to show: "Preview assumes routing policy X; actual calls may hit model Y." Add an `effective_model_hint` plus `policy_applied` metadata to the preview response.

liam: Data model note: deltas should reference filter ids so edits to the base preset propagate correctly. If the base preset removes a filter, routes that did not override it should reflect the removal automatically. If they did override, keep the override. Delta semantics: replace/remove/add with explicit filter ids.

ana: UX for audit/history: surface a changelog entry on the model preset that lists routes affected and show which routes kept overrides. Small timeline with "preset edited" and badges on affected routes would be ideal.

maya: Rollout constraints: we want to canary per-org. Backwards compat: accept legacy flat saved_query objects (scope omitted) and treat them as route-scoped full copies. New orgs default to reference/delta model.

jordan: Feature-flagging plan: server accepts both schemas. Add migration utility that can opt-in to convert copies into references if the org prefers. We'll gate UI features behind the flag.

sam: Testing: add integration tests for combinations: (1) preset edit, (2) route delta present, (3) routing policy override at runtime. Assert preview merge matches actual recorded calls for a synthetic workload. Also add telemetry attribution tests so cost and tokens map to the model actually invoked.

liam: DB storage idea: store deltas as a small array of strings/json blobs (we keep as blobs for flexibility). Keep a version number on presets so we can detect stale references.

kai: Edge-case: when a preset owner renames a filter id or deletes it and re-adds with a new id, we need a reconciliation step. Best effort: when delta refers to missing filter id, mark delta as "orphaned" and surface in diff panel with action required.

ana: Small UX detail: in route list, add a toggle "show inherited settings" which expands a preview of merged filters inline. Defaults off to keep the list compact.

devex-bot: Reminder: update SDK docs for saved_query changes and add an examples page for migrating old saved queries.

maya: OK. Next steps: liam to draft API JSON schema + migration script; jordan to wire feature flag gating and preview endpoint changes; sam to own telemetry integration tests; ana to design diff panel and route-list affordances. We'll reconvene after PRs land. Thanks everyone.
